system.name: HERMES CORE
system.purpose: Publish image originals through the existing Drive-to-GitHub-Actions-to-Supabase pipeline.

system.archive_rule: Use assets[asset_key].archive_folder_id when set; otherwise default_archive_folder_id.

honor-definition.pointer_format: image_asset_id stores the registered arcane_system_assets.asset_key as text.

honor-relief.side_effects: Attaching an image does not select the honor's published variant or change draft/active state.

required_tools.local_file_access: The exact original bytes must be available as a local file path for SHA-256 and Drive upload.

execution.sequence_contract: Follow the exact sequence in features/hermes-core/OPERATIONAL_ACCEPTANCE.md; do not invent a parallel publisher.
execution.queue_trigger: A push to main adding a matching JSON request starts the existing workflow.
workflow_owns: Drive folder and original SHA-256 verification
Image registration and requested target attachment
success_evidence: The HERMES CORE Actions run head_sha equals the request commit.
The workflow completed successfully and its job emitted HERMES_CORE_ACTIVE.
The published Storage path and intended database reference were read back.
The target resolves through features/honors/honors-image-resolver.js when the target is an honor.

failure_policy: If a required tool, permission, folder, contract, or original file is unavailable, name that exact missing item and stop before submission.
Never guess a Drive folder, target UUID, system asset key, or alternate upload route.
Inspect the existing queue, commit, Drive files, run, job steps, and logs before retrying an ambiguous or failed request.
Preserve both Drive originals and never report Inbox receipt or a queue commit as publication success.
Do not create credentials, permissions, migrations, workflows, or another publication path for routine submissions.
secrets_policy: Do not place tokens, private keys, service-account credentials, or image bytes in this manifest or GitHub queue requests.
